query: For titanium alloys used as structural materials, formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could increase surface hardness and wear resistance. Specify the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to the untreated alloy, the service or test conditions under which the effect should hold, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The application of a plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) coating to Ti-6Al-4V alloy will increase its surface hardness and wear resistance due to the formation of a ceramic-like coating.
generation.material_initial_state: Ti-6Al-4V alloy in its untreated state
generation.intervention: Plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) coating with optimized process parameters to achieve uniform coating thickness and properties
generation.conditions: Voltage: 300-500 V, Time: 30-60 minutes, Electrolyte: silicate-based
generation.mechanism: Electrochemical reaction and deposition of a ceramic-like coating
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved surface hardness and wear resistance due to the formation of a hard and wear-resistant ceramic-like coating
generation.boundary: The PEO coating process parameters and the properties of the resulting coating
generation.uncertainty: The optimal PEO coating process parameters and the potential for uneven coating thickness and properties

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the surface hardness and wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V alloy with and without PEO coating
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the PEO coating does not result in a significant increase in surface hardness and wear resistance, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.kind: web:Fabrication of Nano‐Structured 23Fe−21Cr−18Ni−20Ti−18Mn (HEA) Powders By Bal
cited_evidence.text: We have used Retsch Planetary Ball Mill PM 100 to fabricate HEA powders. Initially, the elemental powders such as Fe (99.6 % pure), Cr (99.8 % pure), Ti (99.6 % pure), Ni (99.5 % pure), and Mn (99.2 % pure) of composition 23Fe−21Cr−18Ni−20Ti−18Mn by wt.% were ball milled for 15 hours under toluene atmosphere. The ball‐to‐powder ratios were maintained at 6 : 1 with a mill speed of 300 rpm and the volume of the jar is 500 mL containing the 10 mm diameter chrome steel balls. Toulene was added to arrest the oxidation of the elements and also to aid the milling. Make sure to add toluene in such a way that must just immerse the balls and the elemental powder inside the jar. Ball milling was continued for 15 hours with 30 30‐minute breaks after every 30 minutes of milling; this was done to cool down the temperature of the jar. Generally, during ball milling, the continuous collision of balls‐jar‐powders results in increased temperature inside the jar and may result in phase transformation of the alloy. Therefore, we must allow the ball mill to cool down after every 30 minutes of milling. After 15 hours of ball milling, we have taken out the HEA powders.

The potentiodynamic tests and associated results suggest that the titanium free HEAs are performing better than titanium-based alloys. The EIS test results follow a similar pattern, and it was noted that AlCoCr1.3FeNi1.3 is the best performing alloy for both cases (the logarithm of the corrosion current was ~−5.2 (A/cm2)). We have compared the available data for pure titanium metal where electrochemical corrosion tests were conducted under a NaCl deposit in wet oxygen at 600 °C []. In that case the logarithm of corrosion current value was ~−4.35 (A/cm2) []. In the case of Ti-6Al-4V alloy the log (corrosion current) value in ~1% NaCl was ~−5.75 (A/cm2) []. In case of γ Ti-Al alloy the corrosion current value was ~0.16 (μA/cm2). In the case of accelerated corrosion-based mass loss tests (see Figure A13), the highest loss was noted for alloy 4, namely AlCo0.9CrFeNiMn0.9. Whereas, the lowest loss was noted for alloy 2 (CoCr1.3FeMnNi0.7). This is moreover consistent with potentiodynamic scan test results and associated corrosion currents.

The best wear performance was exhibited by the H-0Nb alloy in the AT-30 condition, with a volume loss of 0.92 mm3, which very low when compared to the value of 3.34 mm3 obtained for the CuBe commercial alloy.
